title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\text{NN}}}$ = 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
summary: Higher-order cumulants ($C_n$) of the event-by-event net-proton number ($ΔN_{\mathrm{p}} = N_{\mathrm{p}} - N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}$) distributions are sensitive observables in the search for the QCD critical point. A reliable quantitative baseline for non-critical effects is essential for interpreting these observables. We calculate $C_2/\langle N_{\mathrm{p}} + N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}\rangle$, $C_3/C_1$, and $C_4/C_2$ in Au+Au collisions at collision energies $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.7$-$27$ GeV with the SMASH hadronic transport model. The collision-centrality, rapidity-window, and collision-energy dependences are reported. The cumulant ratios are predicted below the independent-Poisson baseline, with the suppression increasing toward more central collisions and larger rapidity windows. In 70-80% collisions, SMASH calculations lie above the STAR measurements for all three ratios, whereas in 0-5% collisions, the STAR $C_4/C_2$ value at 19.6 GeV lies below the SMASH reference with a pull of approximately $-2.7$. These results provide an independent non-critical hadronic baseline for assessing the model dependence of the observed data-model discrepancies.

title: Observation of Strong Directed Flow for $φ$ Mesons in the High Baryon Density Region at RHIC
summary: We report measurements of the rapidity-odd directed flow ($v_{1}$) of $φ$ mesons in 10--40\% Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{sNN}=3.0$--4.5 GeV from the STAR fixed-target program at RHIC, together with the collider-energy measurement at $\sqrt{sNN}=7.7$ GeV. Despite its mesonic nature, the $φ$-meson $v_{1}$ exhibits a magnitude comparable to that of protons and $Λ$ baryons and is significantly larger than that of $K^{0}_{S}$ mesons in the high-baryon-density region. Comparisons with UrQMD calculations indicate that the observed $φ$-meson directed flow is consistent with production through high-mass baryon resonances and the collective motion of baryons influenced by baryonic mean-field interactions. These results provide new experimental constraints on baryon-resonance production and strange-hadron transport dynamics in dense QCD matter.

title: Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
summary: Identical charged pion femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions. At high baryon density, the differences between $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ Hanbury Brown--Twiss (HBT) radii may originate from both the third-body Coulomb effect and the initial-state isospin asymmetry. Since the latter is related to the equation of state (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, separating these two effects is essential. In these proceedings, we present the measurements of identical charged pion correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=3.0$, 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, 4.5, and 7.7 GeV collected by the STAR experiment. A correction procedure is developed to remove the residual third-body Coulomb effect. After correction, the extracted HBT radii of $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ become consistent within uncertainties. The results indicate that the observed charge dependence is dominated by the third-body Coulomb effect, while any remaining contribution from the initial-state isospin asymmetry to the relative HBT radius difference, $(R_{π^-}-R_{π^+})/R_{π^+}$, is constrained to be less than 5\% at the 95\% confidence level.

title: Recent Advances and Precision Measurements with the JYFLTRAP Double Penning Trap Mass Spectrometer
summary: High-precision atomic-mass measurements with the JYFLTRAP double Penning-trap mass spectrometer at the IGISOL facility provide direct information on decay energies, nuclear binding and shell evolution, isomer excitation energies, and masses relevant to nuclear astrophysics. Recent work has combined the phase-imaging ion-cyclotron-resonance (PI-ICR) method with established ion-purification and selective ion-production techniques to study low-yield nuclei and resolve isomeric states. At JYFLTRAP/IGISOL, mass-selective buffer-gas cooling, Ramsey cleaning, resonance ionization spectroscopy (RIS), phase-dependent cleaning, and species-resolved PI-ICR analysis are used in complementary combinations according to the ion yield and the required separation. Laser-frequency tagging correlates individual ion events with the corresponding laser frequency and enables state-resolved resonance-ionization spectra. Selected ion bunches are used for direct mass measurements with PI-ICR or time-of-flight ion-cyclotron resonance (TOF-ICR), for ion counting, or for post-trap decay spectroscopy. When multiple species or states are present, resolved PI-ICR phase spots allow the mass-measurement data to be assigned to the corresponding component. Examples from the recent program include high-precision $Q$-value measurements, neutron-deficient nuclei below $^{100}$Sn, neutron-rich fission fragments, rapid structural evolution around $N\approx60$, and rare-earth nuclei relevant to the astrophysical $r$ process.

title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $β$ decays using effective field theory
summary: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $β$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\barδ_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $δV_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.

title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
summary: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_σ$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{σ,{\rm eff}} = 2m_π$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.

title: Ab initio calculations of ${\barδ_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
summary: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $β$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\barδ_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(α^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\barδ_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(α^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $δV_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

title: Beyond the Onsager matrix: All-order resummation of relativistic particle and energy diffusion
summary: We study the coupled diffusion of particle number and energy carried by ultrarelativistic probe particles propagating through a material medium. The probes undergo elastic scattering, which randomizes their direction, and inelastic scattering, which exchanges energy with the medium while preserving particle number. We compute exactly the full $2\times2$ frequency- and wave-number-dependent diffusivity matrix, resumming the constitutive gradient expansion to all orders. In a particularly natural Onsager-normalized basis of conserved densities, the resummed matrix is found to be diagonal at arbitrary frequency and wave number, even though particle and energy transport remain coupled and the conventional Onsager matrix has nonzero thermoelectric cross coefficients. Beyond the hydrodynamic limit, the resummed diffusivities resolve microscopic relaxation timescales and the ballistic kinetic continuum that are invisible to the ordinary Onsager coefficients.

title: $α$--$α$ Correlations in Excited Clustering Nuclei Across the Solid-Liquid Transition
summary: We investigate the structural evolution of $α$-cluster matter using a microscopic transport model for four $α$-conjugate collision systems, including $^{12}\text{C}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{28}\text{Si}+^{12}\text{C}$, and $^{40}\text{Ca}+^{12}\text{C}$ at incident energies ranging from 2.0 to 7.0~MeV/u. The $α$-cluster structure of an excited nucleus undergoes a solid-liquid phase transition with increasing incident energy. Whether it proceeds by the dissociation of individual clusters or by the collapse of their spatial organization remains unexplored, as does the question of whether any characteristic $α$--$α$ correlation survives. The one-body density $ρ(\mathbf{r})$, the standard clustering diagnostic, cannot by itself settle this question, since it neither distinguishes a genuine cluster configuration from a density fluctuation nor reveals the sparse residual clusters masked by the surrounding nucleon medium. We therefore construct the exclusive $α$--$α$ two-body spatial correlation function from the $α$-cluster centroids to isolate the $α$ clusters. In all four systems the $α$--$α$ correlation exhibits two peaks, a nearest-neighbor one and a next-nearest-neighbor inter-cluster one. Both peak positions increase with system size. Over the energy range studied, which spans this transition, the mean number of $α$ clusters per event falls steeply while the $α$--$α$ correlation persists and the inter-cluster distances change only slightly. The individual clusters therefore dissociate rather than lose their spatial organization.

title: Fluctuation modes in the initial state of heavy-ion collisions: from 2D to 3D hybrid simulations
summary: This dissertation investigates how the initial stages of relativistic heavy-ion collisions shape the evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the observables measured experimentally. Particular attention is given to the initial state and pre-equilibrium dynamics, which constitute the main sources of uncertainty in hybrid simulations. The first part of the dissertation reviews the framework underlying state-of-the-art hybrid simulations and the numerical tools used in phenomenological analyses. The second part studies the matching between pre-equilibrium evolution and viscous hydrodynamics. Since commonly used conformal kinetic-theory descriptions are inconsistent with the non-conformal hydrodynamic equation of state, an entropy-density matching prescription is proposed. This prescription reduces the artificial bulk pressure generated at the switching time and improves the consistency of the hybrid framework. The third part develops a mode-by-mode decomposition of initial energy-density profiles to isolate fluctuation modes and quantify their contributions to final observables. Applied to Pb-Pb collisions across centrality classes and extended to a fully three-dimensional O-O collision system, the method shows that initial fluctuations survive hydrodynamic evolution and leave measurable imprints on final observables. In O-O collisions, fluctuations can dominate over geometric effects from the impact parameter, demonstrating that intermediate-sized systems are not simply scaled-down versions of large systems. Overall, these results provide tools for constraining the early stages of heavy-ion collisions and for understanding how fluctuations propagate through the QGP evolution.

title: Wobbling Motion in the Many-Nucleon System
comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, Frontiers in Physics, published
summary: The purpose of this Perspective is not to present a new progress but to shed light on another stream of the study of the nuclear wobbling motion from a viewpoint of the many-body theory under an external field. Special attention is paid to the moments of inertia, which are microscopically calculated as a response of the full $A$-body system to rapid rotations described by the cranked RPA formalism. They depend on the rotation frequency, and it is shown that approach of two moments of inertia leads to the instability of rotating triaxial mean fields.

title: Nuclear Mott transition with neural quantum states
summary: Bound clusters can dissolve in nuclear matter due to Pauli blocking, a phenomenon known as the Mott transition that is a key determinant of the nuclear abundances in heavy-ion collisions. Microscopic descriptions of this behavior require solving the in-medium Schrödinger equation. However, this remains a major computational challenge because the nuclear medium breaks Galilean invariance and couples angular-momentum channels at finite center-of-mass momentum. The emergence of weakly bound states near dissociation further places stringent demands on conventional methods. Here, we address these challenges by introducing MottNet, a momentum-space neural quantum state framework based on self-attention that directly solves the $A$-body in-medium Schrödinger equation. Benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the in-medium deuteron, MottNet reveals substantially weaker Mott suppression for $α$ particles in hot and dense nuclear matter than do conventional calculations based on combined approximations. At high baryon densities, the predicted $α$-particle abundance is enhanced by orders of magnitude, even after continuum-edge subtraction. This finding offers a microscopic explanation for the unexpectedly large $α$-particle fraction inferred from a combined analysis of FOPI heavy-ion collision data and transport model calculations.

title: Pairing connections between localized nuclear regions: Orbital reweighting and thermal quenching
summary: The nucleon localization function (NLF) characterizes nuclear spatial structure; the nonlocal anomalous density (pairing tensor) describes coherent pair amplitude between two points. Global pairing measures leave connections between distinct spatial regions unresolved. We determine how selective orbital participation strengthens pairing connections between localized regions during overall pairing loss, and why heating attenuates the connection while preserving its pattern. Axial Hartree-Fock plus BCS calculations combine NLF with the pairing tensor in shape-constrained 20Ne (distinct localization lobes) and octupole-deformed 144Ba (reflection-asymmetric background). Complete signed orbital sums separate anomalous-weight and spatial-kernel changes at fixed pairing strength and cutoff. Contraction along a constrained 20Ne branch preserves identifiable end lobes while reducing total anomalous norm and increasing the absolute opposite-end integral. Coupled spectrum and gap changes favor a mixed 1d5/2/2s1/2 component and deplete anomalous participation of a predominantly 1p1/2 component. Increased positive strength and weaker destructive interference overcome the net opposing spatial-kernel response; this balance survives mesh refinement. Heating at the reference quadrupole constraint yields compensating thermal and quasiparticle-energy factors, so similar gap reductions produce nearly common attenuation. In 144Ba, octupole deformation and normal-localization modulation persist after anomalous sources vanish. Regional enhancement depends on how selective anomalous participation changes the complete signed orbital sum, including spatial feedback. Nearly proportional participation changes preserve the pattern when kernels remain stable, distinguishing stronger absolute connections from larger normalized fractions on an identifiable localization background.

title: Reduced Density Matrices from Renormalization-Group Flows
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures for the Manuscript; 24 pages, 5 figures for the Supplemental Material
summary: We reconstruct complete one- and two-body reduced density matrices (RDMs) by a single collective backward evolution along the in-medium similarity renormalization-group flow. Benchmarks show improved accuracy and physical consistency over conventional elementwise evolution. In neutron matter, two-body RDMs reveal spin-triplet dominance in interaction-dependent Fermi-sea depletion trends. Meanwhile, the forward-backward energy difference provides an internal diagnostic of many-body truncation errors, whose quantification remains challenging in nuclear $ab\ initio$ calculations.

title: Fast computation of microscopic optical potentials: beyond existing capabilities
summary: A microscopic approach to optical potential calculations, based on the leading term in the spectator expansion of the optical potential operator and carried out in momentum space, has been successful in describing nucleon elastic scattering above 100 MeV. However, high computational cost precludes the inclusion of all physics relevant to scattering, such as the tensor part of the nucleon-nucleon (NN) amplitude, three-nucleon forces, multiple scattering and medium effects. Also, this approach does not provide any nucleon-nucleus scattering wave functions needed for reaction calculations. In this Letter, we develop a harmonic oscillator expansion version of this approach, which provides the same representation of optical potential both in momentum and coordinate spaces, accelerates calculations by two orders of magnitude, includes the missing tensor component of the NN scattering amplitude and is applicable to nuclei with any spin. Test calculations have been performed for several light nuclei whose densities were obtained in the No-Core Shell Model using a chiral Hamiltonian. We demonstrate convergence of this expansion and clarify the role of the tensor force, which manifests itself mainly in coupling between channels with different spin. Comparison to experimental data is presented for selected cases. The methodology could be extended for scattering of other projectiles (hadronic and pionic), small complex nuclei and hypernuclei. It also suggests a pathway for including more complicated physics into the scheme and extending it to lower energies. It could be also helpful in assessing the accuracy of upcoming scattering emulators.

title: Heavy-quark gluon radiation in transversely flowing QCD matter: First-subeikonal corrections
summary: We investigate medium-induced gluon radiation from energetic heavy quarks propagating through a finite-size QCD medium with transverse collective flow. Within the DGLV framework, we calculate the radiation spectrum at first order in opacity and to first-subeikonal accuracy, retaining finite heavy-quark and effective gluon masses. Subleading corrections to the longitudinal propagator poles generate mass-dependent modifications of both the residue denominators and formation phases. For rotationally symmetric transverse-momentum integration domains, all contributions linear in the transverse flow velocity vanish after full azimuthal integration, while a nonzero static first-subeikonal correction remains. For representative medium parameters, this correction increases the integrated fractional radiative energy loss by approximately $10$--$20\%$, depending on the quark mass, initial energy, and path length. At the differential level, transverse flow produces a dipolar angular anisotropy, enhancing radiation along the flow direction and suppressing it in the opposite direction.

title: Open Heavy Flavor in Nuclear Collisions: From Lattice QCD to Observables
summary: Heavy quarks serve as excellent probes of the Quark-Gluon-Plasma (QGP) produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Here, we report on a comprehensive framework that transports charm quarks from their initial production through the QGP medium, hadronization, and the hadronic phase to final observables in experiments. For the transport through the QGP fireball, which is described by 2+1D relativistic viscous fluid dynamics, we employ an extended Langevin equation that combines elastic diffusion processes with medium-induced radiation, including interference effects. The charm-quark transport coefficients are derived from nonperturbative $T$-matrix interactions, which are constrained by lattice QCD and also produce an equation of state for the thermal medium which is consistent with the one employed in the hydrodynamic simulations. Pre-hadronic resonant states which emerge in the $T$-matrix near the QGP transition temperature naturally lead to a transition to hadronic degrees of freedom. This transition is realized in two different approaches: a coalescence model augmented with 4-momentum conservation and the resonance recombination model, both supplemented with fragmentation functions constrained by charm-hadron spectra in proton-proton collisions at the LHC and RHIC. The late-stage rescattering of charm hadrons is assessed with schematic heavy-light cross sections implemented into a hadronic transport model. We report results for the nuclear modification factors and elliptic flows of $D^0$ and $D_s^+$ mesons and $Λ_c^+$ baryons, together with the $D_s^+/D^0$ and $Λ_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios. The calculations are compared with measurements from the ALICE and CMS collaborations in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\NN}}=5$\,TeV and with STAR data in Au-Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\NN}}=200$\,GeV.
